title: The Dream Train
summary: Every night, when the house goes quiet, a train comes to collect the children in their pyjamas and takes them off to dream.

scenes.text:
When the house goes quiet and the lights go out, listen carefully.

From far, far away, over the rooftops, comes a soft whistle.

It's the dream train.

It comes slowly, along tracks made of clouds, and stops right outside your window. It has golden wooden carriages, little lit-up windows, and a chimney that puffs out smoke shaped like stars.

At the door, the conductor is waiting for you. He's an old man with a white beard and a blue cap, holding a lantern.

"Good evening," he says. "Ticket, please?"

"I haven't got a ticket."

"Of course you have," he smiles. "The ticket is a yawn."

And you yawn. An enormous yawn. The conductor punches it with his little machine, click, and lets you climb aboard.

Inside the train, everything is warm and soft. The seats are like pillows, and on each one there's a folded blanket.

There are other children in pyjamas. A girl with a toy rabbit. A boy in dinosaur pyjamas. A baby who fell asleep before the train even left.

The train sets off. Clickety-clack, clickety-clack, very slowly, along the cloud tracks.

The conductor walks down the aisle, seat by seat, and asks every child the same thing:

"Where would you like to dream tonight?"

"To the floating islands," says the girl with the rabbit.

"To count the stars," says the boy in the dinosaur pyjamas.

And the conductor writes it all down in a tiny notebook.

The first stop is the floating islands.

They're little islands hanging in the air, with colourful houses and round trees. One of them has a castle the size of a teapot.

At the station, a little bell rings.

The girl with the rabbit gets off, waves from the platform and skips away over a bridge of clouds.

Then the train climbs. Up and up it goes, to where the stars are so close you could touch them. The boy in the dinosaur pyjamas presses his nose to the glass.

"One, two, three, four…" he starts to count.

When the conductor comes past again, he's fast asleep, with his nose on the glass and his mouth wide open. He had got as far as star number two hundred.

In the end, the conductor stops beside your seat.

"And you?" he asks. "Where would you like to dream?"

You think about it. The islands, the stars, the sea… But your eyes are heavy, and you can't decide.

And you yawn again.

The conductor smiles under his beard.

"I know where you're going."

The train slides gently down through the clouds and stops right outside your window. There's your bed, warm, waiting for you.

"The best station of all," says the conductor.

He tucks you in, turns down his lantern, and you breathe slowly. Once. Twice.

And before the train has even set off again, you're already dreaming.
